paras: The threatened lynching of William Stewart took place near Lafayette, a village north of London, Ohio, in early June 1888, when townspeople threatened to lynch a Black man accused of assaulting a white woman. Stewart had been caught and jailed, and no attack on him is reported. The episode is known from two items in the Springfield daily republic of June 4, 1888.

According to a dispatch from London, Mrs. Flora Byerly, the wife of farmer George Byerly, was washing at their home on the Mellie Marks farm on Darby Creek, three miles north of Lafayette, when Stewart came to the house and asked for a drink. The dispatch said that he made an "indecent proposal," forced his way into the house when she refused, and assaulted her. When she fled, it said, he drew a revolver and threatened to kill her but fell over her small son, and she escaped to the highway, where she fainted.

Stewart got away at first but was caught at West Jefferson by that town's marshal, Baker, and jailed. The dispatch described Lafayette as "all torn up" over the charge. A separate brief in the same paper reported that the "People of Lafayette" threatened to lynch a "negro ex-convict" charged with assaulting two white women.
No report of a lynching attempt, a trial or any later outcome was found.

Both items appeared in the Springfield daily republic on June 4, 1888: the threat as one line in its "Ohio Flashes" column and the assault as a London dispatch headed "An Ex-Convict Assaults a Woman." The dispatch treated the accusation as established, calling Stewart "a burly negro," "the colored brute" and "the scoundrel," and describing the woman's husband as "a respectable and well known farmer." The brief reported the threat without comment, and no other paper's coverage was found.

The two items differ on the charge: the brief said two white women were assaulted, while the London dispatch, which named those involved, described an attempted rape on one woman. Only the brief mentions the lynching threat.

accounts.gist: People of Lafayette threatened to lynch an unnamed Black ex-convict charged with brutally assaulting two white women.

accounts.label: London dispatch
accounts.gist: William Stewart, a Black man, asked Mrs. Flora Byerly for a drink, made an indecent proposal, forced his way into the house and assaulted her, then drew a revolver when she fled; he escaped but was caught at West Jefferson and jailed. The village was 'all torn up', but no lynching threat is mentioned.
